$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
internal/manifest/manifest_test.go in this repository's own CI; `declared`
is a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THE PRODUCT HERE IS A MODULE, AND THE BINARY IS THE SMALLER HALF. Nine
sibling repositories import github.com/TAIPANBOX/agent-stack-go, which is
why C1 in estate-gates watches for a version lag and why `runs: []` is
correct: no deployment installs this, every consumer compiles it in.
SO THE ONE THING THIS REPOSITORY SHIPS AS AN ARTIFACT IS agent-conform, AND
ITS CLAIM IS REPRODUCIBILITY. It decides whether somebody else's payload
conforms, and a verdict is worth what its checker is worth: the person
receiving the verdict has to be able to rebuild the checker and get the same
bytes. Three flags hold that, CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath and -s -w, and they
live in TWO files. ci.yml's own comment says losing one breaks it in
silence, so the check below asserts all three in both places rather than
trusting either.
THE SCHEMAS ARE A COPY AND THE COPY IS THE POINT. cmd/agent-conform/schemas
vendors files TAIPANBOX/agent-passport owns, so the tool is one static
binary and the tests run offline. A copy with nothing comparing it drifts:
on 2026-08-05 the vendored Passport schema was missing SPEC 4.4 and 4.5
entirely, so agent-conform read a mode the spec does not have and printed
OK. schemas-in-sync.sh is what compares them now; this manifest records that
the copy exists and how many files it is, so a schema quietly disappearing
from it is visible here too.

it_is_a_release_artifact_not_a_deployed_.why: release.yml builds it for several platforms so somebody outside this estate can check whether their service conforms. No launcher installs it, which is why estate.json's `runs` is empty and right.

the_module_is_what_the_estate_actually_c.why: Nine sibling repositories import it. That is a dependency rather than an installation, so it is not a component here; C1 in estate-gates is what watches consumers for a version lag.
